title: Archive as Design Employee
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: An archive becomes institutional infrastructure when it is retrievable, interpretable, rights-aware, and capable of changing a live creative decision.
A less-remembered house remains researchable because its object record survives.

01 · RETRIEVE — Can the right record be found?. Identifiers, dates, makers, materials, controlled vocabulary, file relationships, and search pathways determine whether memory is available at the moment of decision.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · READ — Can someone understand why it matters?. A sketch, fitting note, failed sample, or garment becomes more useful when the record preserves the question it answered—not only what it looks like.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · TRANSFORM — Can the archive generate difference?. The strongest use is not literal revival. It is recovery of a method, constraint, construction problem, or unresolved question that can be recomposed for a new context.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · CITE — Can the new work show its lineage?. Source identifiers, rights decisions, credits, and transformation notes let inspiration remain accountable. Citation does not weaken originality; it distinguishes research from extraction.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

mapping.prompt: Select one current design question—not a favorite old object.
Retrieve three records that answer it in different ways.
Record the evidentiary fact and your interpretation in separate fields.
Define what may be reused, what may only be linked, and what requires permission.
